cards.question: What is spaced repetition?
cards.answer: A learning technique where review intervals increase after each successful recall, based on the spacing effect in memory research.

cards.question: What does the SM-2 algorithm use as its quality threshold?
cards.answer: A quality score of 3. Responses rated below 3 reset the repetition count, while 3 or above advance the card to the next interval.

cards.question: Which data structure uses LIFO (Last-In, First-Out) ordering?
cards.answer: Stack — elements are pushed and popped from the top, so the last item added is the first removed.

cards.question: What is the time complexity of looking up a key in a hash map (average case)?
cards.answer: O(1) — hash maps use a hash function to compute an index directly, giving constant-time average lookups.

cards.question: In Python, dictionaries maintain insertion order as of Python 3.7+.
cards.answer: True — since Python 3.7, dict preserves the order in which keys are inserted. This was an implementation detail in 3.6 and became part of the language spec in 3.7.

cards.question: HTTP GET requests should be used to modify server-side state.
cards.answer: False — GET is meant to be safe and idempotent (read-only). Use POST, PUT, or PATCH to modify state.

cards.question: Which sorting algorithm has O(n log n) worst-case time complexity?
cards.answer: Merge sort — it divides the array in half recursively and merges sorted halves, guaranteeing O(n log n) in all cases.

cards.question: What is the easiness factor in SM-2?
cards.answer: A floating-point number (minimum 1.3) that controls how quickly intervals grow. Higher values mean easier cards with longer gaps between reviews.

cards.question: A binary search tree guarantees O(log n) lookup time.
cards.answer: False — only a balanced BST guarantees O(log n). An unbalanced BST can degrade to O(n) in the worst case (e.g., inserting sorted data).

cards.question: Which Python keyword is used to define a generator function?
cards.answer: yield — when a function contains yield, calling it returns a generator object that produces values lazily.

cards.question: TCP guarantees ordered delivery of packets.
cards.answer: True — TCP uses sequence numbers to ensure packets are delivered in order.
